name: 802.11 Wireless Attack Detection — Deauth, Rogue AP & Evil-Twin
description: 802.11 wireless attacks are link-layer threats detectable via monitor mode capture. Deauthentication attacks force clients off the network to capture WPA handshakes or cause DoS. Evil-twin APs mimic legitimate SSIDs to harvest credentials via hostile portals. Rogue APs bypass perimeter controls. Detection requires airodump-ng or Wireshark with 802.11 management frame filters (wlan.fc.type, wlan.fc.type_subtype).
source: CDSA Module 08: Intermediate Network Traffic Analysis
notes:
=== PREREQUISITES: MONITOR MODE ===
# List wireless interfaces
iwconfig

# Enable monitor mode via airmon-ng (kills interfering processes)
sudo airmon-ng start wlan0
  → Creates wlan0mon interface in monitor mode

# Enable monitor mode manually
sudo ifconfig wlan0 down
sudo iwconfig wlan0 mode monitor
sudo ifconfig wlan0 up

# Verify monitor mode
iwconfig wlan0mon   # or 'iwconfig wlan0' if not renamed
  → Should show: Mode:Monitor

=== CAPTURING WIRELESS TRAFFIC ===
# Capture on specific AP channel and BSSID
sudo airodump-ng -c <CHANNEL> --bssid <AP_BSSID> wlan0 -w raw
  → Example: sudo airodump-ng -c 4 --bssid F8:14:FE:4D:E6:F1 wlan0 -w raw
  → Outputs: raw-01.cap (capture), raw-01.csv (data), etc.

# Detect evil-twin by ESSID (shows all APs with same name)
sudo airodump-ng -c 4 --essid <SSID_NAME> wlan0 -w raw
  → Two rows with same ESSID but different BSSID/ENC = evil-twin

=== DEAUTHENTICATION ATTACK DETECTION ===
How it works:
  → Attacker crafts 802.11 mgmt frame with BSSID of legitimate AP
  → Frame type: Deauthentication (type=0, subtype=12)
  → Client cannot distinguish from real deauth without 802.11w
  → Tools: aireplay-ng, mdk4 (default reason code: 7)

Wireshark filters:
# Filter to AP's BSSID only
wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>

# All deauthentication frames from AP's BSSID
(wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>) and (wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 12)

# Deauth frames with reason code 7 (aireplay-ng/mdk4 default)
(wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>) and (wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 12) and (wlan.fixed.reason_code == 7)

# Detect revolving reason codes (sophisticated attacker)
→ Check reason codes 1, 2, 3 sequentially:
(wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>) and (wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 12) and (wlan.fixed.reason_code == 1)
(wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>) and (wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 12) and (wlan.fixed.reason_code == 2)
  → If sequential codes appear = script rotating codes to evade WIDS

Deauth IOCs:
  → Excessive deauth frames sent to a single client MAC
  → Reason code 7 from AP's BSSID = common tool default
  → Rotating reason codes (1→2→3...) = sophisticated evasion
  → Client repeatedly disconnecting and reconnecting

=== FAILED AUTHENTICATION DETECTION ===
# Filter for association/authentication frames
(wlan.bssid == <AP_BSSID>) and (wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 0) or (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 1) or (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 11)
  → type_subtype 0 = Association Request
  → type_subtype 1 = Association Response
  → type_subtype 11 = Authentication

=== EVIL-TWIN / ROGUE AP DETECTION ===
Evil-twin vs Rogue AP:
  → Evil-twin: NOT on network — standalone AP impersonating legitimate SSID
    Purpose: hostile portal (harvest creds), credential capture, MITM
  → Rogue AP: IS connected to network — hotspot or tethered device
    Purpose: bypass network controls, segmentation bypass

Detection with airodump-ng:
  sudo airodump-ng -c <CHANNEL> --essid <SSID_NAME> wlan0 -w raw
  → Legitimate AP: ENC=WPA2, CIPHER=CCMP, AUTH=PSK
  → Evil-twin: ENC=OPN (open) — no RSN information element

Detection with Wireshark beacon analysis:
# Filter for beacon frames
(wlan.fc.type == 00) and (wlan.fc.type_subtype == 8)
  → Open Packet Details → check RSN (Robust Security Network) info
  → Legitimate: RSN present with cipher suites (AES, TKIP, PSK)
  → Evil-twin: RSN absent or mismatched ciphers

# Filter to only evil-twin BSSID
(wlan.bssid == <EVIL_TWIN_BSSID>)
  → Look for client ARP requests — a connected victim shows ARP to DHCP

RSN field differences (expanded in Packet Details pane):
  → Legitimate: RSN Information → Cipher Suites: TKIP, CCMP; Auth: PSK
  → Evil-twin (open): No RSN Information element in beacon frame
  → Check vendor-specific information elements — likely absent from attacker's AP

Response steps:
  1. Record victim's MAC address and hostname from ARP traffic
  2. Initiate password reset for potentially compromised credentials
  3. Locate rogue AP via signal strength + physical search
  4. Disable attacker-controlled AP at switch level if connected

=== 802.11 FRAME TYPE REFERENCE ===
wlan.fc.type values:
  00 = Management frames (deauth, beacons, probe, auth, assoc)
  01 = Control frames (ACK, RTS, CTS)
  02 = Data frames

wlan.fc.type_subtype values (management):
  0  = Association Request
  1  = Association Response
  8  = Beacon
  11 = Authentication
  12 = Deauthentication
  12 = Disassociation

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Enable IEEE 802.11w (Management Frame Protection) — cryptographically signs mgmt frames
  → Utilize WPA3-SAE — stronger auth, harder to crack captured handshakes
  → WIDS/WIPS: detect deauth floods, rogue APs, evil-twins automatically
  → Modify WIDS rules to detect rotating reason codes
